subject: Report span: what moments count? Partial-month inclusivity & point-in-time checks
messages:
From: Acme Audits <audits@acme-audits.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia@clientco.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 coverage question — partial months and point-in-time samples

Hi Logan / Marissa,

Quick follow-up from our planning call: we want to confirm precise inclusivity rules for the upcoming Type II review. Two specific items for ClientCo's assessment: 1) how you treat partial months when a control or service came online mid-month (do we include the entire calendar month or only from the activation timestamp?), and 2) for systems where the evidence is a point-in-time export (e.g., a configuration snapshot), which exact moment should we treat as "the end of day" for that date when compiling population samples (UTC 00:00, local midnight, or the last second of the day in UTC?).

For the sampling work we plan to do, we need an explicit statement so we can finalize our testing dates. If you have an internal bridging practice (bridge letter) for short gaps or transitions, please attach the latest template.

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (past report)

Thanks,
Liam Grant
Engagement Manager
Acme Audits
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Acme Audits <audits@acme-audits.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@clientco.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — partial months and point-in-time samples

Thanks Liam — good questions. Short answers up front: 1) partial months: we treat coverage as inclusive of the exact timestamp the control became effective; we do not automatically bump coverage to the whole month. In practice we provide evidence from the activation timestamp through the period end. 2) point-in-time exports: our operational standard is UTC end-of-day (23:59:59 UTC) unless a customer has explicitly requested local-time reporting; we can provide both if needed.

More context below and I attached a small sample export from 2026-08-31 that shows how we record activation metadata. I also attached a draft bridge letter we can sign for short gaps (bridge_letter_draft.docx).

On partial months: our logs record service-state change events with ISO timestamps; for example, if a feature was enabled at 2026-06-11T14:23:07Z, we will only include evidence from that timestamp onward for that control. For attestations we include a short explanatory statement in the evidence package noting the activation instant.

On point-in-time: our standard snapshot process takes a consistent UTC snapshot at 23:59:59 for every date in the period. If your sampling procedure requires a different cutoff (e.g., customer local midnight), let us know and we can either provide additional exports or map timestamps to the requested timezone.

Attachments: service_activity_sample_20260831.csv, bridge_letter_draft.docx

- Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Customer Compliance 
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Acme Audits <audits@acme-audits.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@clientco.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — partial months and point-in-time samples

Liam / Olivia,

Adding a bit of operational detail from the infra side to avoid confusion during sampling:
- When a control depends on a config change we publish an event with both event_time and effective_time; effective_time is what we use for coverage determinations.
- For rolling changes that cross midnight, our job reconciles by recording the last successful state change for that day; that is what the snapshot CSV contains.
- If the auditor wants inclusive calendar months despite activation timestamps, we can produce a one-line attestation that treats the service as covered from the start of the month (we prefer timestamp accuracy but will accommodate client/auditor preference).

If you confirm which approach you want for ClientCo sampling (timestamp-accurate or calendar-month inclusive), we'll prepare the appropriate packaged exports and the signed bridge letter for any gaps under two weeks.

Neha Kapoor
Security Controls Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Acme Audits <audits@acme-audits.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia@clientco.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage question — partial months and point-in-time samples

Thanks all — that helps a lot. For ClientCo we will: 1) use the activation timestamp as the inclusion boundary for controls that clearly have an effective_time, 2) use 23:59:59 UTC as the point-in-time cutoff for snapshot evidence unless ClientCo confirms local-midnight is required, and 3) accept a signed bridge letter for any gaps under 14 days.

Olivia, please confirm if you want us to treat any specific months as calendar-inclusive (ClientCo has a known migration that straddled June>July). If not, we'll proceed with timestamp-accurate sampling and schedule the fieldwork for the week of Sep 20.

Best,
Liam Grant
Engagement Manager
Acme Audits
